## Packages

[sRtr](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/sRtr) supplies the region geography and the transplant-center download, so the original scripts' own data files are no longer needed [@srtr_package]. sf handles the spatial data. ggplot2 draws the main version of each map, and tmap (version 4) draws the version with an inset of the Washington-Boston corridor. colorspace provides the `OrYel` palette the published maps used.

```{r}
#| label: load-packages
#| eval: false
```

## Constants

- `map_crs` is the projection every layer is put in before plotting: NAD83 / Conus Albers (EPSG:5070), the projection sRtr stores its region data in.
- `corridor_extent` is the area enlarged in the tmap inset, in longitude and latitude: the Washington-Boston corridor, from DC to Boston, where centers crowd together.
- `adult_center_exceptions` are the two centers with "Children" in their name that the original maps kept because they also transplant adults.
- There is no data path: each study's regional counts are written out in its own script.
- `label_margin` is the gap, in metres, kept between the corridor box and the region numbers placed beside or inside it.
- `center_label` and `map_note_template` are the legend entry for the center dots and the note printed under every map; `{retrieved}` in the note becomes the date the HRSA layer was downloaded.
- `figure_width`, `figure_height`, `base_text_size` and `tiff_dpi` size the saved maps for a double-column journal figure: 7 by 4.6 inches, 8-point text, TIFF at 600 dpi.
